issues.t: Four-speed automatic slips or fails
issues.sym: Slipping, flaring RPM between shifts, late or harsh shifts, lost gears (often 3rd, 4th or reverse), or burnt-smelling fluid.
issues.why: Vans of these years use GM's 4-speed automatics (4L60-E on lighter vans, 4L80-E on heavy-duty). Heavy loads and heat wear the clutches, and the 4L60-E's sun shell is a known weak part.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and smell. If it slips, stop hauling heavy loads and get a transmission shop diagnosis. A transmission cooler helps vans that work hard.

issues.t: Intake manifold gasket leaks coolant
issues.sym: Coolant level drops with no obvious leak, the engine runs hot, oil looks milky, or there is a sweet smell.
issues.why: The original intake manifold gaskets on the Vortec 4.3L, 5.0L and 5.7L engines break down with heat and age and leak coolant outside or into the oil.
issues.next: Watch the coolant level. If it keeps dropping or the oil turns milky, stop driving and have the gaskets replaced before the bearings are damaged.

issues.t: Central "spider" fuel injector sticks or leaks
issues.sym: Rough idle right after a cold start, long cranking, misfires and a check engine light.
issues.why: These Vortec engines use one central injector unit with small poppet valves feeding each cylinder. Deposits make them stick, and the unit can leak fuel inside the intake.
issues.next: Have misfire codes and fuel pressure checked. Replacing the central injector unit usually fixes it.

issues.t: Fuel pump keeps failing
issues.sym: The van cranks but won't start, stalls, or loses power under load. Some owners replace the pump more than once.
issues.why: The electric fuel pump in the tank wears out; owners of 1997 and 1999 vans report repeated failures.
issues.next: Have fuel pressure tested. Replace the pump module and check the wiring connector so the new pump isn't damaged.

issues.t: 4.3L V6 burns oil
issues.sym: Needing a quart or more of oil between changes, blue smoke at startup, or fouled spark plugs.
issues.why: The 2003-2014 4.3L V6 is widely reported for excess oil use, worst on 2004-2009 engines.
issues.next: Check the oil level every fill-up and top it off. If use is heavy, have the PCV system and rings checked.

issues.t: Broken exhaust manifold bolts
issues.sym: A ticking or tapping noise from the engine that is loudest when cold, and sometimes an exhaust smell.
issues.why: Exhaust manifold bolts on GM's 6.0L V8 snap from repeated heating and cooling, letting exhaust leak.
issues.next: Have it repaired before the leak burns the gasket or nearby wiring. Shops often fit stronger bolts.

issues.t: Duramax diesel overheats when working hard
issues.sym: Temperature gauge climbs while towing, on hills or in hot weather; the engine may cut power.
issues.why: The LLY Duramax diesel is known for limited cooling capacity under heavy loads.
issues.next: Ease off and let it cool. Keep the radiator and intercooler clean and have the fan clutch checked.

issues.t: Clogged diesel particulate filter
issues.sym: Frequent regeneration, loss of power, a DPF or check engine light, and rising oil level from fuel getting into it.
issues.why: The LMM Duramax was GM's first diesel with a particulate filter. Short trips and idling clog it, and extra fuel used to clean it can thin the oil.
issues.next: Drive at highway speed regularly so the filter can clean itself, and change the oil on time. A shop can force a regeneration or clean the filter.

issues.t: Diesel high-pressure fuel pump failure
issues.sym: Sudden stalling, no-start, or loss of power, sometimes after a long crank. Metal debris can be found in the fuel.
issues.why: The 2011-2016 Duramax uses the Bosch CP4 high-pressure pump, which can fail internally, especially with water or poor fuel, and spread metal through the fuel system.
issues.next: Use clean fuel and change fuel filters on time. If it fails, the whole fuel system often has to be cleaned or replaced.

issues.t: 8-speed automatic shifts hard, slips or won't go into gear
issues.sym: Hard downshifts, slipping, harsh low-gear upshifts, trouble shifting from Park or Reverse into Drive, or transmission failure.
issues.why: GM has issued bulletins and a customer satisfaction program for the 8-speed automatic, including valve body check balls that wear and stick, and a machining flaw in some valve bodies. Owners report failures around 50,000-60,000 miles.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check your VIN for open programs and software updates. Have shifting problems looked at early, before the transmission is damaged.

issues.t: Transmission software can cause harsh shifts or wheel lockup (recall)
issues.sym: Harsh shifting, loss of power, sudden slowing, rear wheel lockup or unexpected movement.
issues.why: Incorrect transmission control software was installed on some vans.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. A Chevrolet dealer does recall repairs for free.

issues.t: Fuel pump control module fails and engine stalls
issues.sym: Hesitation, jerking or stalling while driving, sometimes with no warning light; steering and braking get heavy once the engine dies.
issues.why: The module that powers the fuel pump can fail and cut fuel to the engine. GM opened a program to inspect and replace it on 2025 vans.
issues.next: If the van stalls, get safely off the road. Ask a dealer about program N252526151 and check for the fuel pump module codes.

issues.t: Transmission fluid leak
issues.sym: Red fluid spots under the van or a low transmission fluid level.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin telling technicians to add dye to the fluid to find the exact source of transmission leaks on these vans.
issues.next: Have the leak traced before parts are replaced; running low on fluid can ruin the transmission.

issues.t: Drive belt squeals or breaks
issues.sym: Belt squeal, a hard start or no-start, or sudden loss of power steering and brake assist if the belt breaks.
issues.why: GM issued a repair bulletin for these symptoms on its full-size vans (Express and its twin, the GMC Savana).
issues.next: Have the belt, tensioner and pulleys checked if you hear squealing. A broken belt makes steering and braking much harder, so pull over safely.

issues.t: Driver door impact beam may be poorly welded (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs; the door may protect less in a side crash.
issues.why: The impact beam inside the driver's door may have bad welds. Dealers replace the door.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. A Chevrolet dealer does recall repairs for free.

issues.t: Passenger head restraint may be poorly welded (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs; the head restraint may not protect well in a crash.
issues.why: The front passenger head restraint may be badly welded to the seat frame.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. A Chevrolet dealer does recall repairs for free.

issues.t: Steering gear nut may not be tightened (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking, play or a loose feel in the steering. In the worst case the van can lose steering control while driving.
issues.why: A nut on the steering gear may not have been tightened correctly at the factory on some 2025-2026 Express and Savana vans built from January 2025 to June 2026. GM later issued a second recall to recheck vans that were not inspected properly the first time.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls, even if the first steering recall was already done. If the steering feels loose or clunks, don't drive the van; have it towed to a Chevrolet dealer. The inspection and any steering gear replacement are free.

issues.t: 2.8L diesel turbo whine or oil at turbo ducts
issues.sym: A whining or whistling noise that rises with engine speed, or oil around the intercooler ducts.
issues.why: GM bulletins cover turbo replacement for bent turbo blades and a loose charge air cooler duct clamp that lets oil seep from the turbo ducts.
issues.next: Have the turbo and ducts inspected. A loose clamp is a simple fix; a damaged turbo needs replacing.

issues.t: ABS module fails and replacement parts are scarce
issues.sym: ABS and traction control lights come on, the ABS kicks in at low speed, or the van pulls to one side when stopping.
issues.why: Owners report repeated ABS module failures on these vans, and several say GM had no replacement module available.
issues.next: Normal brakes still work, but drive carefully on slick roads. Ask shops about rebuilt modules if a new part isn't available.

issues.t: Brake line can rub on a body mount
issues.sym: A brake fluid leak or soft pedal from a line worn through where it touches the body.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin to find and repair a brake line that may contact a body mount.
issues.next: Have the brake lines inspected; a worn line can leak and cause a loss of braking.

issues.t: Driver window switch can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: Window switch stops working, a burning smell or smoke from the driver's door.
issues.why: Liquid can leak into the driver's power window switch, corrode it and cause a fire risk. Dealers replace the switch.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. A Chevrolet dealer does recall repairs for free.

issues.t: Rear climate control can short and overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke near the rear climate controls in the headliner.
issues.why: A wiring short at the rear climate control module could overheat and start a fire in the headliner.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. A Chevrolet dealer does recall repairs for free.

issues.t: Unused rear heater wiring can overheat on cutaway vans (recall)
issues.sym: A burning plastic smell or melted wiring near the driver-side door pillar. There may be no warning before damage.
issues.why: On Express cutaway chassis (the base for box trucks, shuttle buses and RVs), wiring for an optional rear heater and A/C blower is often left unused. Its exposed connectors can corrode, overheat and start a fire. About 150,000 Express and Savana cutaways were recalled.
issues.next: If your Express is a cutaway, check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. A Chevrolet dealer seals the unused circuit at the driver-side door pillar for free. If you smell burning, pull over and have it checked before driving further.

issues.t: Tires may lose tread or blow out (recall)
issues.sym: A bulge in a sidewall, vibration, or sudden air loss.
issues.why: Some original tires were over-cured at the factory and can break at the sidewall or separate.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. A Chevrolet dealer does recall repairs for free.

issues.t: Battery cable can short against the fuse block (recall)
issues.sym: Possible burning smell or electrical problems; the risk is a fire. GM advised parking outside until repaired.
issues.why: The positive battery cable terminal may touch a fuse block post and short-circuit.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. A Chevrolet dealer does recall repairs for free.

issues.t: Transmission can drop into neutral
issues.sym: The transmission suddenly goes into neutral and the van loses drive power.
issues.why: A fault in the transmission's internal range sensor could put it in neutral; GM's service update reprograms the transmission computer.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check your VIN for service update N192282860; it is free.

issues.t: Van can roll away after leaving Park (recalls)
issues.sym: The shifter moves out of Park without pressing the brake, or the key comes out while not in Park.
issues.why: Faults in the shift interlock let the van leave Park without the brake or with the key out.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. A Chevrolet dealer does recall repairs for free.

issues.t: Alternator voltage regulator can short and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: Burning smell or smoke from the engine area, or charging problems.
issues.why: An internal short in the voltage regulator could get hot enough to start a fire.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. A Chevrolet dealer does recall repairs for free.

issues.t: Transmission defect can strand the van (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden loss of drive, leaving the van stopped on or near the road.
issues.why: A transmission defect on some 2008 vans could cause a loss of drive.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. A Chevrolet dealer does recall repairs for free.

issues.t: Steering linkage or wheel bearing nuts may loosen (recalls)
issues.sym: Wandering or loose steering, grinding from a wheel, or the ABS light, with the van pulling to one side.
issues.why: Some 2003 vans had pitman arm, tie rod or wheel bearing nuts that were not tightened properly.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. A Chevrolet dealer does recall repairs for free.

issues.t: Brake booster seal can fail (recall)
issues.sym: A harder brake pedal that needs more effort to stop.
issues.why: An O-ring seal in the brake booster valve could fracture.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. A Chevrolet dealer does recall repairs for free.

issues.t: Rusted fuel filler pipe can leak (recall)
issues.sym: Fuel smell or fuel leaking near the filler while refueling.
issues.why: The fuel filler pipe can corrode and leak, creating a fire risk.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. A Chevrolet dealer does recall repairs for free.

issues.t: Power steering cooler hose can leak onto the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Power steering fluid leak, a burning smell or smoke from the engine compartment.
issues.why: A defective power steering cooler hose could spill fluid onto hot engine parts and start a fire.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. A Chevrolet dealer does recall repairs for free.

issues.t: Fuel odor or fuel leak (recall)
issues.sym: A raw fuel smell or fuel dripping under the van.
issues.why: Fuel could leak near an ignition source on some 1996 vans.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. A Chevrolet dealer does recall repairs for free.
